description: Zero-dependency graph layout engine that renders to text: DAGs and cyclic graphs (dashed back edges), clusters, four flow directions, colors. no_std + no-alloc capable, from servers to microcontrollers.
rules: Build graphs with Graph::new(), add_node(id, content), add_edge(from, to, Option<&str> label); then g.compute_layout() and ir.render_string(&RenderOptions::plain()). Tune layout with LayoutConfig and g.compute_layout_with_config(&config).

0.11 removed the 0.9-era render_scanline* wrappers and the SugiyamaConfig surface (Graph::compute_layout_with, set_sugiyama_config, with_sugiyama_config), and the `warnings` cargo feature. Use render_string / render_with / render_to_bytes, LayoutConfig, and typed diagnostics; the mapping is in docs/migrate-from-0.10.md (0.9 users apply docs/migrate-from-0.9.md first).

Feature flags: std, alloc, generic, layout-vertical (TopDown/BottomUp), layout-horizontal (LeftRight/RightLeft), arena, arena-idx-u8/u16/u32, ports. With default-features = false at least one layout axis is required; disabled Direction variants do not exist, and the default direction is TopDown when vertical is enabled, else LeftRight. `ports` is a default feature and links nothing when off.

For no_std/embedded: an allocation-backed Graph converts via to_csr before compute_layout_arena; TRUE no-alloc construction builds directly with CsrGraphBuilder, then compute_layout_arena and render_to_bytes, with buffers sized by estimate_csr_arena_size / estimate_layout_arena_size / estimate_render_arena_size / estimate_render_output_size (see examples/lean_render.rs and examples/longan_nano). Enable `arena` plus at most one arena-idx override; u8/u16 index widths use 16-bit cell coordinates. The arena layout also uses stack outside those estimates (about 16 KB on 32-bit targets in 0.11) - budget for it on 32 KB-class parts; see BENCHMARK.md.

All four rank directions: TopDown, BottomUp, LeftRight, RightLeft (parse from "TB"/"BT"/"LR"/"RL"). Heap Graph users call set_direction or set LayoutConfig.direction; arena/CSR users set LayoutConfig.direction. LeftRight and RightLeft are native sideways layouts, not transposes.

RenderOptions is three parts: plan (PlanOptions: palette, style callbacks, label_policy), emit (EmitOptions: charset, color_mode, render_legend) and compose (ComposeBudget). Presets: plain(), colored(palette), ascii(), ascii_colored(palette). An edge label that fits nowhere inline is omitted by default and reports W.Render.Label.031; to keep and print such labels set plan.label_policy.overflow = LabelOverflow::Legend AND emit.render_legend = true - enabling the legend alone does not recover omitted labels.

Non-fatal events are typed diagnostics, never stderr. Convenience: g.layout().reported() returns an OwnedReport whose warnings() iterates Diagnostic values (code(), Display) and whose outcome() holds the LayoutIR. No-alloc and custom collection use DiagnosticRun with a sink (VecDiagnostics, CountingDiagnostics, SliceDiagnostics, FnDiagnostics, IgnoreDiagnostics) through the diagnostic-aware entry points; codes are stable strings such as W.Graph.Node.021. See docs/diagnostics.md.

Introspection is the scene model: create a planner with ScenePlanner::new() (or ScenePlanner::new_in(&mut [u8]) for a caller-sized workspace). planner.plan(&ir, &options.plan) returns a pending PlanRun, not a Scene; finish with .quiet()? to obtain a Scene while discarding diagnostics, .compute(&mut cx)? to collect diagnostics in a caller-owned run, or .reported() to obtain an owned report whose outcome must be handled. A successful Scene borrows the planner and the layout. Scene exposes nodes(), edges(), subgraphs(), node(id), legend(), dimensions and hit-testing; SceneComposer streams one CellView per canvas cell; TerminalRenderer renders one Scene repeatedly with different EmitOptions without replanning. Size no-alloc workspaces with ir.estimate_scene_size(&PlanOptions) and scene.composition_requirements(&budget). See docs/rendering.md.

Ports (feature `ports`): declare attachment sides on an edge with .from_port(side) / .to_port(side) on the handle add_edge returns. Sides are the compass (North/East/South/West, fixed on the page) or the flow (Upstream/Downstream/Clockwise/Counterclockwise, which follow the direction); Auto is the default. Port placement policies: set_port_policy (graph) / set_node_port_policy (node) choose Paired, Spread or Custom. The IR reports requested and resolved sides; an unhonored side is a diagnostic (W.Graph.Port.034/035). See docs/ports.md and examples/ports.rs.
Node content is an impl NodeContent: plain &str for [label] nodes, BoxedNode for 3-row boxes, CustomNode for custom sizes and painters.
Cyclic input: the compute_layout() pipeline reverses back edges internally and renders them as dashed return lines; the legacy Graph::render() convenience instead prints a cycle banner.
The complete per-item API reference lives at https://docs.rs/ascii-dag - fetch it (or read the vendored crate source) for signatures and items not covered by these guides.
